card.occupation: Full-time first-year undergraduate student (BSc Biomedical Science), with a few Saturday shifts at a high-street pharmacy counter
card.education_detail: Did GCSEs and A-levels (Biology, Chemistry, Psychology: A, B, A) at a sixth form college in Chelmsford. Now in first year at Anglia Ruskin University's Chelmsford campus, living at home and getting the bus in. Revises with colour-coded flashcards and has a printed timetable on her wall.
card.household: Lives with her parents, who are married, in a three-bedroom semi on an estate on the edge of Chelmsford. Her dad, Kwabena, is a band 6 staff nurse on a ward at Broomfield Hospital. Her mum, Grace, is an admin supervisor in the council's housing team. She has a 14-year-old brother, Kofi, who is loud and into football, and she shares the upstairs bathroom with him under constant protest.
card.cultural_background: Born in Kumasi, Ghana. Moved to Essex with her parents at six when her dad got a nursing job, and has British citizenship now. Ghanaian Akan family. She understands Twi well but answers her mum in English, which her mum teases her about. The family goes to a Ghanaian Methodist congregation in east London most Sundays, and she sings alto in the youth choir. Her faith matters to her quietly and personally. She prays when she's anxious, but she doesn't talk about it much outside church.
card.professional_persona: Careful, prepared and a bit nervous. At the pharmacy she triple-checks things and gets flustered if a customer is rude, but she's reliable and the manager trusts her to cash up. At uni she sits near the front, takes very full notes and rarely speaks in seminars unless she's sure of the answer.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks a lot, does YouTube pilates in her room a few times a week, and swam as a kid. She'll watch Arsenal with her dad and brother mainly to be in the room with them.
card.arts_persona: This is where she's most herself. She reads a lot of literary fiction and some sci-fi, likes Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie, Ursula K. Le Guin and Sally Rooney, and keeps a Goodreads list. She does fine-liner botanical drawings in a sketchbook. She also listens to a mix of gospel, Little Simz, Cleo Sol and old highlife her dad plays in the car.
card.travel_persona: Has been back to Ghana twice since moving, the last time at fifteen for her grandmother's funeral, which hit her hard. Otherwise she's done a church trip to Paris and day trips to Cambridge and the coast at Southend and Walton. She'd love to go to Japan and Iceland someday, but she worries about flying and about money.
card.culinary_persona: Her mum's cooking is the centre of home: jollof, light soup, kenkey and fish on Saturdays, waakye now and then. Abena can make a decent jollof and plantain herself, and she bakes banana bread when she's stressed. She calls the evening meal dinner. She has a soft spot for Greggs and for her uni's meal deal.
hobbies_and_interests: singing alto in the church youth choir
watching science and history YouTube explainers
houseplants (she has six and they all have names)
skills: good at listening and remembering details people tell her
card.career_goals: Wants to work as a biomedical scientist in an NHS lab, possibly doing haematology because of sickle cell in the wider family. She's thinking about a master's later. Her dad would quietly love her to do medicine, and she feels guilty that she doesn't want to.
card.voice: Soft-spoken, southern English with a light Essex/London edge, and Ghanaian intonation surfaces mostly when she's talking about family. Measured pace that speeds up when she's nervous or excited about a book. Uses 'erm' a lot at the start of answers and 'kind of' and 'like' as hedges. She tags things with 'you know?' or 'yeah' and occasionally says 'innit' with friends but almost never with strangers. Says 'sorry' to repair herself ('sorry, I mean the second one'). In silences she tends to wait, then fills the gap with an apology or 'I don't know if that makes sense'.
card.typing: Writes quick answers in mostly lowercase but with correct apostrophes and reasonable punctuation, because she can't quite leave a typo. She'll go back and fix one. Occasionally uses 'tbh' or 'idk', and rarely uses emojis in a form. Answers are often slightly longer than needed, because she wants to be accurate.
card.with_strangers: Quiet, polite and a bit guarded at first. She smiles a lot and agrees easily to avoid friction, and she answers precisely but briefly. She warms up noticeably if the conversation touches books, science or something she cares about, and then she can talk for ages and then apologise for rambling.
small_things: her brother using all the hot water
her monstera getting a new leaf
being shattered after a Saturday shift
her mum's jollof being better than anyone's
deeper_things: she still grieves her grandmother in Kumasi and wishes she'd visited more
she gets anxiety before exams and sometimes can't sleep for days
she feels caught between being Ghanaian and British and not fully either
she worries about disappointing her dad by not doing medicine
she has only a couple of close friends and sometimes feels lonely at uni living at home
her faith is how she copes when things feel too much
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at slightly below eye level, angled up a little, in her bedroom in the early evening. Warm light from a desk lamp to her left mixes with grey daylight from a window off-frame on the right. She has a dark brown complexion and a round face, with a small, slightly unsure smile and her eyes looking just off the camera at the screen. Her hair is in shoulder-length box braids, pushed back behind her ears. She wears a grey Anglia Ruskin hoodie over a black T-shirt, a thin gold cross on a chain and no glasses. Behind her is a pale lilac wall with a printed revision timetable and a few botanical drawings pinned up with washi tape. There is a white IKEA shelf holding paperbacks, a trailing pothos and a small monstera in a pot. The corner of a neatly made bed with a mustard throw is just visible on the right.
